topology: PC1 enters R1. The R1–R2–R3 triangle provides a preferred path through R2 and a direct higher-delay R1–R3 backup. SRV1 is on R3; R2 Loopback0 is an independent control destination. Physical links, addressing and HTTP are prepared. R3 initially runs classic AS200 while R1/R2 use100.
implemented: Ninth ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry with independent practice/completed factories, five-row plan, staged guide, tested reference and IOS/Windows verification commands, current-site domain/path/query permalinks and accurate accessible section counts. All prior entries remain available.

Initial diagnosis requires three actual PC1/R2-loopback replies and three PC1/server No route drops at R1 with the exact AS200 mismatch and only the R1/R2 adjacency. The repair removes the wrong process and recreates classic AS100 with the intended router ID, networks, passive policy and no auto-summary.

Each restored router must have two UP EIGRP peers. The intended R1 server and R3 client routes are internal D, AD90, metric10240 and CEF next hop through R2. R2 learns each directly attached remote LAN at metric7680. A lost-UPDATE counterfactual proves configuration and Hello/INIT alone cannot install server reachability.

Bidirectional host delivery requires three destination-accepted requests and parent-linked delivered replies in each direction, with actual routed sends through R2. HTTP requires the complete actual200 response and expected service body on the preferred request path; a wrong200 page cannot earn it.

The passive exercise keeps the R1/R2 physical port up but removes its adjacency. The converged R1 server route uses the direct R3 neighbor with metric261120, and three real requests must take that path. Restoring the active exception requires preferred route convergence and fresh bidirectional delivery.

Removing only R3 server network membership keeps all six directional neighbors UP and the local connected server LAN intact, but delivered withdrawals remove the R1/R2 service routes. Three real No route failures and independent control successes precede restoration and fresh traffic.

The K-value exercise changes R3 coefficients from1/0/1/0/0 to1/0/0/0/0. Both R3 neighbors disappear while R1/R2 and the diagnostic prefix remain. Actual server failures and control success are required before restoring default weights and bidirectional service. Hello/hold timer equality is not presented as an adjacency requirement.

A temporary R1 inbound prefix distribute-list excludes the server route from both peers while all neighbors remain UP and R2 retains its own service route. The exercise distinguishes filtering received route information from an interface packet ACL. Removing both binding and temporary list plus fresh traffic earns repair.

Changing only R1 backup-interface delay1000 to15 selects a working direct request path at metric8960 while R3 continues to prefer its10240 R2 return route. Actual direct-path replies precede restoring delay1000, converging to the intended preferred routes and fresh bidirectional traffic. The chosen comparison remains within the exercised feasibility conditions; no hitless or guaranteed feasible-successor switchover is claimed.

Thirteen tasks combine five live process/neighbor/route/health/save checks and eight observations. Practice starts0/13. The completed reference supplies5/13 without invented diagnosis, traffic, HTTP or repair evidence. Historical observations survive YAML export/import; current health and startup equality revoke on drift.

Per-attempt config and route epochs plus normal simulator notifications collect synchronous CLI evidence with a closed guide. Queries, two probes, configuration-only toggles, server power loss, static shortcuts, named-mode substitutions, rewiring and unsaved drift cannot satisfy the prescribed outcomes. No networking engine, protocol implementation, UI styling, terminal theme or artwork changed.
scope: Classic IOS IPv4 internal EIGRP in one AS after repair. This is simulator/native/browser validation against published Cisco behavior, not a fresh CML capture or wire-compatible Cisco implementation. It excludes named mode, IPv6, authentication, redistribution, variance, SIA, BFD and guaranteed hitless/feasible-successor convergence; existing engine boundaries remain documented in docs/audits/eigrp-update-fidelity.md.
